# Engineering Invariants

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_invariants.py; edit invariants.json. -->

A project activates only the invariants its real capabilities require and
records each current rung using the enforcement ladder.

| # | Invariant | Activates when | Default rung | Owning skills |
| -: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **`canonical-authority`**: Every fact has one authoritative owner, and every semantic behavior has one canonical implementation path. | always | `owner` | `architecture-foundations`, `application-composition` |
| 2 | **`bounded-contracts`**: Modules expose small intentional contracts; storage, provider, and framework internals remain behind their owners. | a module or process boundary exists | `local_check` | `architecture-foundations`, `interfaces-and-events` |
| 3 | **`shared-semantics`**: Shared product semantics live below every UI, API, worker, assistant, and backend; differences live in adapters. | two surfaces implement the same product behavior | `fault_test` | `application-composition` |
| 4 | **`explicit-composition`**: Assembly occurs in an explicit composition root rather than ambient globals or route construction. | a system has replaceable dependencies or multiple adapters | `local_check` | `architecture-foundations`, `application-composition` |
| 5 | **`durable-admission`**: When accepted user intent must survive the caller, successful admission means that intent is already durable. | work may outlive a request, route, process, or device opportunity | `fault_test` | `durable-workflows` |
| 6 | **`normal-failure-semantics`**: Retries, duplicates, timeouts, cancellation, interruption, and process death are defined execution paths. | work crosses a temporal or process boundary | `fault_test` | `durable-workflows`, `interfaces-and-events` |
| 7 | **`committed-event-truth`**: Events come from committed facts; durable consumers use persisted delivery or recovery state, while ephemeral events only wake them. | events or notifications can affect correctness | `fault_test` | `interfaces-and-events`, `durable-workflows` |
| 8 | **`publication-classes`**: Material data, operation progress, operation terminal state, and connectivity or authentication are distinct publication classes. | events invalidate reads or update user-visible operation state | `local_check` | `interfaces-and-events`, `application-composition` |
| 9 | **`coalesced-bounded-work`**: Equivalent intent coalesces, and concurrency, memory, network, provider, and queue use are explicitly bounded. | work can repeat, fan out, or consume shared resources | `fault_test` | `durable-workflows`, `interfaces-and-events` |
| 10 | **`transient-presentation`**: Presentation owns rendering and transient interaction, not retries, synchronization, imports, provider polling, or durable workflow state. | an interactive client exists | `local_check` | `application-composition` |
| 11 | **`useful-paint-graph`**: Every important surface has an explicit useful-paint graph; optional enrichment loads and fails independently. | a user-visible surface performs asynchronous reads | `fault_test` | `application-composition` |
| 12 | **`persistence-qos`**: Interactive persistence receives priority, while noninteractive work is bounded, observable, and yields between committed units. | interactive and background work share a non-preemptible resource | `fault_test` | `durable-workflows`, `application-composition` |
| 13 | **`authority-context-fencing`**: Durable operations capture stable account or tenant authority at admission and fence every commit, acknowledgment, and publication. | active authority can change while work is in flight | `fault_test` | `durable-workflows`, `data-and-compatibility` |
| 14 | **`representation-separation`**: Source observations, canonical state, projections, caches, transport objects, and persisted records remain distinct representations with explicit owners. | one fact has more than one representation | `owner` | `data-and-compatibility`, `architecture-foundations` |
| 15 | **`explicit-deletion`**: Absence is not deletion; destruction requires an explicit lifecycle event such as a tombstone, erasure, or verified lossless migration. | state is synchronized, imported, repaired, or migrated | `fault_test` | `data-and-compatibility` |
| 16 | **`versioned-compatibility`**: Persistent, wire, event, storage, and worker contracts are versioned; temporary compatibility names consumers, proof, telemetry, and a removal gate. | independently deployed readers and writers coexist | `ci_check` | `data-and-compatibility`, `verification-and-operations` |
| 17 | **`typed-boundaries`**: Identity, time, units, provenance, capability, and privacy are validated boundary types rather than conventions hidden in strings. | ambiguous primitives cross a trust or representation boundary | `local_check` | `interfaces-and-events`, `data-and-compatibility`, `application-composition` |
| 18 | **`discoverable-operations`**: Humans and agents use one discoverable operational interface; machine configuration is local and secrets remain in credential systems. | the repository has repeated build, test, migration, repair, or release actions | `ci_check` | `verification-and-operations` |
| 19 | **`separate-action-authority`**: Implementation, integration, metadata change, deployment, installation, migration, repair, and publication are separately authorized actions. | work can mutate shared or external state | `runtime_guard` | `verification-and-operations` |
| 20 | **`typed-exact-evidence`**: Claims bind to exact revisions and evidence classes; generated, simulated, automated, physical, and production observations never substitute for one another. | a result gates integration, release, compatibility, safety, or physical behavior | `ci_check` | `verification-and-operations`, `architecture-hardening` |

The default rung is a starting recommendation, not a claim about a
repository's current enforcement. The project profile records reality.
